cells.tense: The reaping is here now, and your hands are on it.
cells.act: let the inner compass decide the small case
cells.ask: Settle an owed thing by your own sense of what is fair — decided alone, done without a word to anyone.
cells.core:
What you waited on is showing itself now, and your hands are on it. You can look over what grew and stay honest about the yield — part of it is what you meant, part isn't, and neither needs an argument. Fairness is running clear in you: what's owed and what isn't, known without grinding through the arithmetic. Nobody watching changes how it gets called.

Use that on something with a small tilt — a debt, a favor, an apology you keep meaning to make. Let the private sense of right call it, then act with no witness and no announcement. Small calls like that are how the compass stays true for the large ones. What gets settled quietly stays settled, and the light you steer by stays clean.
cells.sheetLine: What you waited for is here, and you know how to weigh it.
cells.verb: Gathering what patient change has grown
cells.place: where you steer by what you actually want

cells.tense: You will have already tallied the harvest before it is fully in.
cells.act: spend an hour with the thing you love without a task attached to it
cells.ask: Give an hour to something you love with nothing asked of it — no list, no verdict, no fixing anything after.
cells.core:
The fields are being read before they finish ripening. The crop is still coming in, and the verdict is already written — what it proves, what it says, what should have gone differently. That isn't assessment anymore; it's judgment running past what's actually here. The pull toward what you want is being used to measure instead of to steer by.

Give the reading nothing to do for an hour. Whatever the heart holds can be there without a list or a conclusion, and it can stay unfinished a while longer. If a verdict is still needed after that, it will be the truer one. A crop counted twice in the same week counts the same; counted too early, it counts wrong.
cells.sheetLine: You're judging the yield before it's finished coming in.

cells.tense: You stood at the field edge and the harvest is still out there.
cells.act: find the rhythm and stay in it
cells.ask: Take the piece you keep circling without picking it up, and do one round of it at a steady pace.
cells.core:
The work happened — planting, waiting, all of it — and the field got ahead of you somewhere in there. What grew is still out there, and gathering it isn't happening. The pull toward what you want has gone quiet, sitting on the far side of a door you already walked through.

Move where wanting and doing can go the same way, and pick a speed you could keep for a month. Something modest: the piece you keep circling without picking up. Do that much, the same way twice. Momentum here doesn't want a shove; it wants a rhythm your feeling can carry. Sort it a row at a time, and the ease comes back into the moving.

cells.tense: You are deciding what this all meant while insisting you decided nothing.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: Lay out your own frame once — what you kept from this year, what you let go, and why — before anyone asks you to explain it.
cells.core:
The crop got weighed by a hand that's yours, and your name isn't on the scale. The outcome gets called luck, timing, other people, the season — while what got kept and what got let go was settled here. The pull toward what you want is working through you; described, it sounds like something that happened to you.

Name the frame you've actually been using, out loud, before it's asked for: what stayed, what went, and the reason. Claim the deciding as yours. A structure that's named stays honest and stays yours; unnamed, it needs the denials to hold it up. Say it once, and nothing about the yield changes — the hand on the scale just stops being invisible.
cells.sheetLine: You set the order of this year while saying it happened to you.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the case is already closed in the Balanced cell ('you can tell which of it was actually yours') — the record says what the medicine is free to feed next, not that anything has been settled. A reader could fairly say the harvest is still emotional and nothing about it is clear yet; if so, the ask (one case, decided alone, paid quietly) still stands and still costs only a private decision. The line that serves the writer more than the person is 'the harvest is yours to keep,' so it stays out.
